Subject: Pricing exhibit redlines from Procurement (initial)

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is our procurement team's markup of Exhibit B (pricing schedule) with comments around package anchoring, the proposed floor, and the cap language. Two key asks from our side:

- Can you explain the rationale for the 12-month minimum floor in Section 3.b? Our usage profile is seasonally lumpy and committing to that floor for yr1 will push us over budget.
- We want clearer language on how credits/true-ups are calculated if actual usage falls below the floor — specifically we need a 90-day reconciliation window and a cap on retroactive invoices.

We also propose smoothing the discount tiers so the step from Band 1 to Band 2 is not a cliff (procurement's concern is revenue recognition volatility).

Attached: brite-pricing-exhibit_redlines_v1.pdf (PDF; 42KB)

Can your team propose a set of redlines we can review with legal? We need to get to a shared draft for our GC by next week.

Best,

Team — forwarding BriteHealth's markup. Quick context: high-priority expansion deal, ARR profile looks attractive but they push back hard on first-year minimums. Procurement wants a 90-day reconciliation window and softer tier jumps.

Ask: can we craft an internal compromise that balances our minimum-revenue protection and their request for flexibility? My initial ideas:

- Offer a "ramp" for the first 12 months: floor reduced to 80% of committed minimum for yr1 with a true-up across months 10–12 (not retro beyond 90 days).
- Add a "shelf capacity" clause that converts unused committed tokens in Q1 to a one-time credit applied in Q4, capped at 25% of the unused amount.
- Smooth tier thresholds by introducing a micro-band between Band 1 and Band 2 (e.g., Band1: 0-250k, Micro: 250k-400k, Band2: 400k+). This helps avoid cliffing while preserving economics.

Laura/Marissa: can legal/commercial draft language for Exhibit B that covers the ramp + 90-day reconciliation + credit cap? Karthik, can you run the numbers on revenue impact (yr1 / yr2) and propose the precise percentages?

I'll keep Sara on copy so procurement sees progress, but let's treat this as internal until we have an agreed text to send formally.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Thanks Logan — ran the modeling against the proposed ramp and micro-band. Attached is a suggested commercial redline that preserves ~92% of our projected yr1 revenue while addressing BriteHealth's budget concerns. High-level:

1) Year 1 floor: set to 80% of committed minimum for the first 12 months; any shortfall triggers a true-up that is limited to the 90-day reconciliation window following the end of month 12. No retroactive invoices before that 90-day window.
2) One-time shelf credit: convert up to 25% of unused committed tokens in Q1 into a credit that must be used within the same 12-month term; credit calculation follows the net unit price at the time of purchase.
3) Micro-band smoothing: insert a 150k micro-band between Band1 and Band2. Price within the micro-band is linearized; we propose using a blended rate to avoid a step-change.
4) Cap language: move from a hard annual cap to a per-invoice cap equivalent to 120% of the monthly forecasted maximum to avoid surprise billing for them but preserve our exposure limits.

Attachment: redline_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF; 18KB) — contains the redline markup for Exhibit B with tracked changes and commercial footnotes.

I flagged two items that will need legal input: (a) how to phrase "linearized pricing" so it's enforceable for billing, and (b) the exact mechanics of the credit conversion formula (gross vs net).

If everyone agrees, I can send this version to Sara as a non-binding commercial proposal and request their GC's review.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer

Logan/Karthik/Marissa —

Thanks for the draft. I reviewed redline_proposal_v2.pdf and have the following legal comments to keep the language administrable and limit future disputes. High-level changes in the attached docx.

Key legal redlines:

- Section 3.b (Minimum Commitment / Floor): Replace "Customer shall be liable for" with "Customer shall be invoiced for, and Redwood may charge" to preserve invoicing discretion and collection rights while avoiding absolute enforcement language that procurement will push back on.

- True-up window: Accept 90-day reconciliation but add a clear notice period: any true-up invoice will be issued within 60 days after reconciliation close and customers have 30 days to dispute. This provides a deterministic timeline for both parties.

- Shelf credit mechanics: Define the credit as "non-refundable, non-transferable" and require notice of election to convert within 45 days after Q1 close. Limit the credit application so accounting can map to a single invoice (avoids amortization questions).

- Micro-band linearization: Legal wants a formulaic definition rather than "blended rate". Proposed clause: "Rate within the Micro-Band shall be calculated by linear interpolation between Band1 and Band2 unit prices based on actual usage in the Micro-Band."

- Cap / surcharge protections: Add language limiting cumulative additional charges (including surcharges) to no more than 10% of the annual committed value unless mutually agreed in writing. This guards against unexpected invoice spikes and should be acceptable commercially.

Attachment: exhibit_b_legal_markups.docx (DOCX; 24KB) — includes tracked changes and comment bubbles for specific lines.

Please confirm you want us to send this version to BriteHealth or whether we'd prefer a separate "commercial only" cover email that frames these as compromise terms. If we send to procurement, I suggest adding a short bullet table in the covering email summarizing the operational mechanics (timelines, dispute process, credit election).
